title: Gabriel–Zisman calculus of fractions (localization criterion)
body_html:
Gabriel–Zisman localization criterion

Proposition [Gabriel–Zisman, §1.3]. Let $F : \mathcal{A} \to \mathcal{B}$ be a functor with right adjoint $G$, and let $\Sigma$ be the class of morphisms in $\mathcal{A}$ that $F$ sends to isomorphisms. If the counit $\mathrm{counit}_B : F G(B) \to B$ is an isomorphism for every $B \in \mathcal{B}$, then $F$ induces an equivalence $$\mathcal{A}[\Sigma^{-1}] \;\xrightarrow{\;\sim\;}\; \mathcal{B}.$$

This is the abstract category-theory engine behind both Cosh_G(X,R,φ)[Σ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_φ(G) (§3 Cor) and Coeff_G(B(Σ), Φ)[E_Φ⁻¹] ≃ Rep_Φ(G) (§7.4 Thm): combine an adjunction with a counit-isomorphism statement (the resolution theorem) and get a localization equivalence for free.

The relevant references are §1.3 Prop 1.3 parts (ii) and (iii) of the Gabriel–Zisman book.
